decision_conditions: The application fails to demonstrate that the outbuilding is ancillary to the main dwellinghouse, and the introduction of a separate, self-contained residential unit to the rear garden conflicts with policies which require householder development to be subservient to the main dwellinghouse. The outbuilding includes the facilities required for day-to-day living and has separate access, with no functional link to the main dwellinghouse. It fails to reflect the surrounding context and would compromise the character and amenity of the area. The proposal represents an inappropriate and uncharacteristic residential form in a rear garden setting which results in harm to the character and context of the area.  As such, the proposal is contrary to: National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (December, 2024)Policy D4 of the London Plan (March, 2021)Policies SP2, DMD1 and DMD5 of The Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September, 2024) The Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (February, 2012)

The proposed development would be at odds with the surrounding pattern of development and would result in harm to neighbouring occupiers through generation of noise, disturbances and comings and goings as a result of the residential use. The development would therefore constitute unneighbourly development and is contrary to:National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (December, 2024)Policy D4 of the London Plan (March, 2021)Policies DMD1 and DMD5 of The Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September, 2024)The Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (February, 2012)
description: Construction of a single storey rear extension and a single storey rear outbuilding to be used as an annexe ancillary to the main dwelling
borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
